articleTitle: Nonlinear System Modeling Based on Wavelet Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Currently., the modeling of nonlinear systems has garnered widespread research interest. In this paper., a wavelet neural network (WNN) based on Mexican Hat wavelet functions for precise identification of nonlinear system dynamics is proposed. First., a radial basis neural network (RBFNN) with Mexican Hat wavelet functions as the kernel function is designed to enhance the accuracy of nonlinear system modeling. Second., by computing the Euclidean distance between system states and grid points., the grid points were optimized., enhancing the computational performance of the algorithm. Third., to accelerate the convergence speed of the identification error., a switching function for the identification error was defined. Finally., the new algorithm was compared with existing deterministic learning algorithms. Experimental results indicate that the wavelet neural network can achieve more accurate identification of nonlinear dynamic systems.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Compliance Detection for Power Enterprises Based on NLI and LLM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Enterprise compliance refers to ensuring that a company's operations adhere to relevant laws, regulations, industry standards, and internal policies. Non-compliance can result in legal liabilities, financial losses, and reputational damage, making it a critical issue in corporate governance. With the advancement of generative artificial intelligence, particularly Large Language Models (LLM), the potential for automated compliance analysis is emerging, offering new methods and tools for enterprise compliance detection. This paper proposes a two-stage compliance detection framework that combines Natural Language Inference (NLI) models and LLM to enhance the efficiency and interpretability of compliance detection between corporate policies and higher-level laws. The framework leverages NLI models for efficient reasoning in detecting semantic conflicts, while LLM are used to generate natural language explanations for deeper semantic analysis, thereby improving both the accuracy and interpretability of compliance detection. Experimental validation in the power industry demonstrates that the proposed framework significantly enhances detection efficiency and reduces compliance risks.

articleTitle: Classification of Cognitive Activities EEGs via Singular Spectrum Analysis and Joint Approximate Diagonalization of Eigen-Matrices Algorithm with Ensemble Classifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Cognition involves the recognition and perception of external objects to solve creative problems and adapt to the environment, forming the foundation of human intelligence. However, neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD) lead to cognitive impairment. Transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) is a recognized therapy for enhancing cognitive performance. This paper proposes using singular spectrum analysis (SSA) and the joint approximate diagonalization of eigen-matrices (JADE) algorithm with an ensemble classifier to classify electroencephalograms (EEGs) before and after TENS application during various cognitive activities. Initially, subjects wear a headband to acquire single-channel EEGs before and after TENS is applied to their radial nerves. Empirical mode decomposition (EMD) is then used to suppress underlying EEG trends. Subsequently, SSA and the JADE algorithm perform blind source separation (BSS) of EEGs from electromyograms (EMGs) and electrocardiograms (ECGs). JADE is a fourth-order based independent component analysis (ICA) algorithm. The tunable Q-factor wavelet transform (TQWT) decomposes EEGs into subbands from which features are extracted. Finally, an ensemble classifier, combining random forest and least squares support vector machine (LS-SVM), classifies the data. The computer numerical simulation results demonstrate that our proposed method achieves higher classification accuracy compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: Vertical Displacement of Slab End Detection and Quantification Based on Multidimensional Information Fusion of Point Cloud
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: The detection and quantification for vertical displacement of slab end (VDSE) is critical in infrastructure construction for ensuring project quality and construction safety, etc. Traditional reliance on manual measurement is inefficient, and using the method without multidimension to address this challenge is a significant limitation. To this end, we propose an end-to-end method for VDSE detection and quantification through point cloud with multidimensional information. Firstly, we transform the 3D point cloud into a 2D depth map to detect the location of the VDSE and record the its pixel coordinates. Secondly, we reverse-project the VDSE 2D coordinates to the space 3D coordinates, and split the raw point cloud into two subsets based on the spatial position of the VDSE. Finally, we fuse 2D and 3D information and propose a planar phase method to quantify the VDSE. Experimental results show that our method achieves 85.50/0 precision, 91.3% recall and a maximum 16.4% error for VDSE detection and quantification, providing valuable insights and strategies for addressing analogous challenges in infrastructure construction.

articleTitle: Interpretable Semantic-aware Unsupervised Segmentation of Skin Lesions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Segmenting skin lesion images presents significant challenges due to the irregular morphology of lesions, com-plex backgrounds, and blurred boundaries. While traditional manual pixel-level annotations are precise, they are also labor-intensive and costly. This necessitates the development of efficient unsupervised lesion segmentation techniques. In this study, we introduce a simple yet effective framework that employs readily available generative adversarial networks (GANs) to leverage interpretable semantic directions within the latent space for unsu-pervised lesion segmentation. By reframing the disentanglement of semantic directions as a semantic space reconstruction task, our approach eliminates the reliance on supervised information. This shift removes the need for extensive manual annotations during training, without compromising segmentation accuracy. Extensive experiments on a large dataset of dermoscopic images demonstrate that our framework significantly improves both lesion synthesis and unsupervised segmentation. Remarkably, our approach achieves a 6-point Dice score improvement over the supervised U-Net model. Additionally, the proposed framework is adaptable to various GAN backbone networks, producing segmentation outputs that exhibit enhanced realism, sharper contours, and superior boundary delineation accuracy. This study paves the way for more cost-efficient and accurate skin lesion segmentation, with potential applications in automated dermatological diagnostics and beyond.

articleTitle: Classification of EEGs via Multi-layer Wavelet Transform and Feature Fusion to Enhance Depression Screening
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: It is worth noting that depression is a serious mental illness, and early diagnosis and treatment are crucial. This study aims to achieve automatic screening for depression by analyzing electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. However, EEG signal processing faces various challenges with noise. To solve this problem, we propose an adaptive threshold-based multi-layer wavelet transform (MWT) denoising method. This method combines the multi-scale decomposition properties and adaptive threshold processing technology. It retains the high frequency information of the signal while reducing noise interference. In order to compensate for the information loss after signal denoising, this experiment uses fusion features to integrate multiple information to help restore and retain the characteristics of useful signals, thereby enhancing the performance of the classification model. For the purpose of the experiment, EEGs of four subjects with depression and five healthy subjects were first obtained when they performed five activities. The classification results verified the effectiveness of the method in improving the classification accuracy, classification sensitivity, and classification specificity of depression. The classification accuracy of this method is as high as 87.68<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>• In addition, the non-invasive EEG acquisition headband used in this study is simple and easy to use, suitable for a variety of occasions, and provides a feasible solution for large-scale screening and early intervention of depression.

articleTitle: MSEDOA: Enhancing DOA Estimation with Multiscale Squeeze-and-Excitation Networks for Automotive Millimeter-Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Direction-of-Arrival (DoA) estimation is a critical task in automotive millimeter-wave radar systems, enabling the localization of targets and the implementation of essential safety functions. Traditional DoA methods struggle under low SNR and limited snapshot conditions. To address these challenges, we introduce MSEDOA, a novel deep learning method that processes raw IQ signals with a neural network featuring multiscale feature extraction, channel attention mechanisms, and Squeeze-and-Excitation Residual Networks. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms traditional DoA estimation methods, providing precise estimates in challenging environments.

articleTitle: Optimizing Renewable Energy Heating: An Integration of TRNSYS Simulation of Solar and Ground Heat Exchange Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: To address global energy shortages and carbon emissions, exploring efficient and sustainable heating solutions has become a major research focus. This study evaluates a direct heating system that couples solar collectors with medium-depth ground heat exchangers (MDGHE) using TRNSYS simulation software to achieve 100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> renewable energy heating. By integrating solar collectors, the system's heating capacity is significantly enhanced, effectively compensating for the limitations of medium-deep geothermal energy alone. The study demonstrates that a hybrid heating system combining solar collectors and MDGHE not only meets heating demands but also substantially reduces reliance on traditional auxiliary heating, achieving the goal of fully renewable energy-based heating.

articleTitle: A Method for Target Locking in Combat Process Based on the Enhanced YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Rapidly locking onto combat targets during the bat-tle process is an important capability for accomplishing combat missions in modern warfare. The YOLO series of algorithms can effectively meet the needs for this capability during combat operations. However, in military missions, there are complex battlefield environments, and the YOLO series of algorithms has issues with missed and false detections during night combat operations. To address this issue, this paper proposes a target locking method during combat based on an improved YOLOv8, the improved YOLOv8 model is referred to as KAN-YOLOv8n. In this method, the original Conv layer in the C2F module of the YOLOv8 algorithm is replaced with a KolmogorovArnold Networks (KAN) convolutional layer, creating a new C2F-KAN module. The KAN convolutional layer has the characteristic of a learnable nonlinear activation function, which can extract the features of targets under complex conditions with higher accuracy and speed after multiple iterations. The experimental results on the Thermal Tank Images dataset show that the method proposed in this paper can effectively improve the accuracy of target detection, with an mAP50 of 65.8%, which is 8.7%, 14.9%, and 14% higher than that of YOLOv6n, YOLOv8n-world, and YOLOv9c, respectively.

articleTitle: Self-organizing Recurrent Fuzzy Neural Network for Nonlinear System Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Recurrent fuzzy neural network (RFNN) are widely used with nonlinear system modeling. However, the modeling ability of RFNN is usually compromised due to the presence of uncertain external disturbances and changing unknown environments. To address this problem, a self-organizing recurrent fuzzy neural network with modified Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm (MLM-SORFNN) is proposed for nonlinear systems modeling. Firstly, a dynamic adjustment mechanism of the network structure based on correntropy is proposed to improve the network ability to adapt to uncertain environments. Secondly, an improved LM algorithm with adaptive learning rate is designed, which can improve the modeling accuracy while ensuring the convergence of the network. Finally, the experimental results demonstrate the superior modeling capability of the MLM-SORFNN.

articleTitle: Wind Turbine Gearbox Temperature Prediction Based on the DSCNN-BiLSTM Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: The health of the gearbox is critical for the safe and stable operation of wind turbines, with its operating temperature serving as a reliable indicator of gearbox condition. However, due to the non-linearity and complexity of temperature signals collected in real-world applications, traditional prediction methods often struggle to accurately forecast the actual operating temperature of wind turbine gearboxes. To address this challenge, this paper presents a novel deep learning model designed to predict temperature fluctuations in wind turbine gearboxes and evaluate their health status. The proposed model integrates a Deep Separable Convolutional Neural Network (DSCNN) and a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) network, combining strong spatial and temporal feature extraction capabilities. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms four existing models in terms of temperature prediction accuracy, exhibiting superior adaptability and sensitivity, thereby providing a more effective approach for gearbox health monitoring in wind turbines.

articleTitle: Optimal Multi-channel Denial-of-Service Attack Towards the Consensus of Multi-Agent Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: This paper explores the refinement of multi-channel denial-of-service (MCDoS) attack strategies towards the consensus of multi-agent systems (MASs). Initially, we model a consensus-oriented MAS. Subsequently, we describe the MCDoS attack methodology applied in our study. By integrating the attacker's energy expenditure with the system's consensus error as the optimization objective, we introduce an optimization method to minimize it, thereby identifying the optimal MCDoS attack strategy. The paper concludes with a simulation example that demonstrates the effectiveness of our proposed approach.

articleTitle: DBCERT: Reconstruct the BERT Model for Chinese Spelling Correction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Chinese spelling correction (CSC) constitutes a research field of high practical significance. However, most studies proposed a large number of auxiliary modules to fulfill the design goals, resulting in increased complexity in the model structure and the number of parameters. In this paper, we propose a model named DBCERT, which constructs detection and correction modules by reconstructing BERT, endowing it with strong capabilities to perceive and correct spelling errors. Additionally, similarity samples are proposed to train the model's ability to perceive the similar relationship between characters. Without adding any auxiliary modules, DBCERT achieves excellent Chinese spelling correction performance, which represents a significant improvement compared to other works.

articleTitle: Abnormal Vibration Detection by $2\mathrm{D}$ Digital Image Correlation Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: In industrial IoT, sensors are embedded in machinery to monitor critical factors such as bearing wear, motor degradation, and environmental conditions. Traditional sensor-based IoT setups are costly and invasive. With the advancements in computer vision, image-based defect detection has made significant progress across various domains. This study proposes to integrate deep learning, via a high-speed camera, with DIC (digital image correlation) techniques for non-intrusive, full-field anomaly detection of a vibrating object, such as industrial motors. Through image processing, the surface of the vibrating object is partitioned into sub-regions, each undergone FFT analysis. By combining the results from all sub-regions, the normal/abnormal state of the vibrating object is determined. Experimental results demonstrate the feasibility of this approach. We also contribute a dataset with detailed annotations collected from our experimental environment for future work.

articleTitle: Exploring How Urban Morphology Influences Building Thermal and Environmental Performance Alongside Renewable Energy Utilization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: This research addresses the critical challenge of understanding the complex interactions between urban morphology and building thermal efficiency, particularly within the context of urban heat islands and energy consumption. The study employs a parametric approach, using advanced simulation tools within the Grasshopper environment (Ladybug, Honeybee, Dragonfly, and Wallacei) to assess how urban design parameters-such as window-to-wall ratio (WWR), building orientation, density, and number of floors-affect energy consumption and thermal performance. The novelty of this research lies in its framework, which integrates real-time urban microclimate data into these simulations, enabling a more comprehensive analysis of energy dynamics in urban settings. This integration allows for a more accurate understanding of how various design decisions-such as increasing building density or optimizing orientation-impact energy efficiency and the intensity of urban heat islands.

articleTitle: Recurrent Omnidirectional Stereo Matching Method Based on Mixture of Laplace Loss
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Recurrent Omnidirectional Stereo Matching (RomniStereo) is an effective method to estimate omnidirectional depth. At present, most of the depth estimation methods ignore the distortion of the fisheye images, which has a negative impact on the performance of the algorithm. To deal with distortion at the edges of the fisheye image, a new mixture of Laplace loss function is used in the network, which add the uncertainty estimation of the pixels on the fisheye image in traditional loss function. Uncertainty estimation can effectively distinguish the distortion degree of fisheye images, so as to improve the depth estimation effect under the condition of large distortion. There are three important parameters in loss function are predicted and updated through loops for greater accuracy. Experimental results show that the proposed method generates excellent results in both synthetic and real-world environments, and the distortion at the edges of the fisheye image has been effectively improved.

articleTitle: Application of the MOD-STL-Louvain Method for Community Detection in Manufacturing Industries: A Study on Electricity Consumption
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Electricity consumption data captures the usage patterns across various regions, industries, and enterprises, acting as a crucial indicator of economic activity and growth potential. Therefore, analyzing electricity consumption data is essential for understanding economic development. This paper introduces a novel method, MOD-STL-Louvain, for exploring the clustering patterns of enterprises based on their electricity consumption data. The method combines STL decomposition, complex networks, and the Louvain community detection algorithm to classify enterprises into different communities according to their electricity consumption trends. The method was applied to the electricity consumption data of several industries in a province in Eastern China, and the results showed that it can effectively classify enterprises into different communities, which can be characterized by different electricity consumption trends. This research provides a new perspective for understanding the development status of enterprises in their industries and offers a valuable reference for economic work.

articleTitle: Classification of Motion Imagination via Multivariate Variational Mode Decomposition and Second-Order Blind Identification Using Multi-Channel Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: BCI devices based on motor imagery classification can significantly improve the quality of life for paralyzed patients. However, with the advancement of medical devices, clinical equipment is evolving towards portable devices, which have far fewer channels than clinical equipment. Portable devices can collect both Electroencephalogram (EEG) and magnetoencephalograms (MEG). Most current techniques are not suitable for low-channel data or are only applicable to either EEG or MEG. To address these issues, this paper proposes a classification method based on multivariate variational mode decomposition (MVMD) combined with Second-Order Blind Identification (SOBI). First, MVMD decomposes the original multi-channel signals into various components, and then SOBI is used to denoise these components. Next, multiple features such as mean, and fractal dimension are extracted from the clean components. Finally, classifiers like SVM are used for classification. On EEG and MEG datasets, classification accuracies of 74.2% and 82.5% were achieved, respectively. Compared to other advanced methods, our approach achieved higher classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Adaptive Control for Nitrate Nitrogen with Time Delays Based on Recurrent Fuzzy Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: The wastewater treatment process is a sophisticated operation characterized by pronounced nonlinearity, uncertainty, and time-delay properties. The nitrate nitrogen concentration is identified as the primary challenge in meeting total nitrogen standards. To achieve precise control, an adaptive control method based on a recurrent fuzzy neural network with time delays is proposed. Initially, the recurrent fuzzy neural network is utilized to effectively identify the unknown dynamic parameters in the wastewater treatment process. Subsequently, the time-delay model of the denitrification process is established, and the Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional is applied to mitigate time-varying delays. Finally, the stability of the designed controller is theoretically proven. By utilizing Benchmark Simulation Model 1 simulation, the superior control performance is further verified.

articleTitle: Application of Air Quality Monitoring for 3D Printing Process
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: As the popularity of Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) 3D printing continues to grow, there is an increasing need to ensure the health and safety of those working with these technologies. The printing process can release a variety of airborne particulates and volatile organic compounds (VOCs) that may be harmful if not properly monitored and controlled. This paper explores the development of automated air quality monitoring systems to enhance the safety and sustainability of the FDM 3D printing workflow. The key challenges of manual air quality monitoring, such as the lack of real-time data, limited spatial coverage, and disruption to the workflow, are discussed. The benefits of automated air quality monitoring, including improved efficiency, enhanced safety, regulatory compliance, and process optimization, are then presented. The paper delves into the design of an effective automated air quality monitoring system, highlighting the importance of selecting appropriate sensors capable of accurately detecting pollutants, and the need for real-time data visualization and reporting capabilities. The implementation of such a system can significantly improve the 3D printing environment, protecting worker health and ensuring regulatory compliance while enabling process optimization for better output quality.

articleTitle: Privacy Preserving Prescribed-Time Formation Algorithm of Multi-UAV Systems with Event-Based Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel privacy-preserving prescribed-time formation algorithm for multiple unmanned aerial vehicle (multi-UAV) systems, where a high-gain controller with event-triggered design is developed. In our framework, the initial positions of the UAV s are assumed to be private, and each uses some deterministic signal to conceal its real initial states before broadcasting them over the communication network. Consequently, the proposed algorithm is demonstrated to be efficient in guaranteeing successful formation of the UAV s in the specified time without disclosing their real initial data. The controller is shown to be bounded in spite of the high-gain, and the event-trigger helps to reduce the redundant update of the controller, exhibiting no Zeno behavior. Finally, a numerical example is given to verify the validity and effectiveness of the proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: An Analytical Study on Toy Age Grading Methods: A Comparative Study of Large Language Models and Machine Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: This research delves into the utilization of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Machine Learning (ML) in age grading assessments within the toy industry. It compares the efficacy of these methodologies in establishing suitable age ranges for toys, a critical aspect for ensuring child safety and compliance with regulations. LLMs, harnessing pretrained models, enable swift evaluations through visual and textual inputs, yielding instant results with minimal human intervention. Conversely, ML models necessitate training on labeled datasets to gauge age appropriateness, presenting opportunities for ongoing improvement with updated data. A comparative analysis between a trained ML model and GPT 3.5 Turbo unveiled differ accuracies and readiness in age grading assessments. While LLMs offer rapid insights, ML models shine in scalability and the refinement of accuracy over time. The study's findings highlight the strengths and limitations of each approach, proposing customized applications for stakeholders in the toy safety and development domain based on their distinct requirements and resources.

articleTitle: Research on Surface Defect Detection of Aluminium Based on Improved Faster RCNN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Aiming at the problems that the traditional detection algorithm does not have a high recognition rate of defects on the surface of industrial aluminium and is inaccurate in locating small defects, an improved Faster RCNN deep learning network is proposed to detect eight kinds of defects on the surface of aluminium. Firstly, the feature pyramid network (FPN) structure is added to the backbone network to enhance the feature extraction capability for small defects, then the ROI Align algorithm is used instead of the rough ROI Pooling algorithm to obtain more accurate defect localisation information, and finally, the multi-attention mechanism is integrated into the feature extraction part to improve the detection accuracy of PenLiu and CaHua, with 12% improvement for PenLiu and 14.7% improvement for CaHua. The experiments show that the mean average precision mean value (mAP50) of the improved network for the detection of surface defects in aluminium is 88.58%, which is 6.23% higher than that of the original Faster RCNN network, and the ability to detect small defects in aluminium is also significantly improved.

articleTitle: Legal Judgement Prediction via Contrastive Learning Based-Retrieval and Semantic Embedding
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Legal judgment prediction is a significant task in Legal Artificial Intelligence, aiming to predict judgment results based on fact descriptions automatically. The judgment output may include law articles, charges, prison terms, or combinations. Relevant legal cases with similar backgrounds or events should likewise be considered essential references for judgment, as they play an indispensable role in evaluating the prediction task. However, when applied to Chinese legal data, current methodologies often neglect the specialized preprocessing required for unique semantic attributes of Chinese, which affects their prediction performance. This paper proposes a novel contrastive learning- based model for legal judgment prediction named CLR-LJP to improve prediction performance. According to the legal judgment process in real life, law article prediction is converted as a multi- label classification task that includes both relative law cases and law articles. The CLR-LJP firstly converts fact descriptions, law articles, and charges into vectors by embedding Chinese semantics. Then, contrastive learning is introduced in retrieval training to distinguish the similar content of different label definitions. Finally, the role embedding method is applied to learn the interactions among multiple law articles to predict prison terms. Experiment results indicate that our CLR-LJP model achieves the best performance compared to the state-of-the-art models, especially in the task of prison term prediction.

articleTitle: DNN-Based Task Partitioning and Offloading with Reliability Guarantees in Multi-UAV-Assisted MEC System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) applications based on Deep Neural Networks (DNN) have gained widespread attention in mobile edge computing (MEC). However, it is still challenging to ensure reliable transmission and meet delay-sensitive requirements in dynamic networks. In this paper, a multi-UAV-assisted MEC architecture is designed, where multi-ple UAV s are endowed with computing offloading services for the mobile devices (MDs). To guarantee reliable communication in highly dynamic scenario, we formulate the robust transmission problem, and leverage the conditional value-at-risk approach to analyze the successful transmission probability in the worse-case channel condition. On this basis, to accelerate the inference of DNN, we formulate the Collaborative DNN Partitioning and Offloading (CDPO) problem by presenting a collaborative DNN partitioning and offloading scenario, which is NP-hard. Further-more, we introduce a highly effective Collaborative Partition and Offloading Optimization (CPOO) algorithm based on the Bat algorithm to solve the CDPO problem. In addition, considering both reliability-guaranteed and delay-sensitive requirements, we propose the master problem as a non-convex optimization prob-lem and the LaCPOO algorithm, which combines the sub gradient algorithm with the CPOO algorithm. Simulation results demon-strate that compared to other algorithms, our proposed approach can accelerate DNN inference while ensuring reliability.

articleTitle: Classification of Cognitive EEGs via Attention-Based Multi-Scale Dilated Convolution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Cognitive ability refers to an individual's psychological capacity and level demonstrated in activities such as thinking, memory, and learning. The transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) is widely regarded as a therapeutic method for improving cognitive ability. Therefore, this paper proposes a framework based on EEG signals to evaluate the effectiveness of TENS therapy in cognitive enhancement. Specifically, this paper uses Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT) to convert EEG signals into time-frequency diagrams, while Phase Space Reconstruction (PSR) is employed to transform EEGs into phase space matrices. Subsequently, both the time-frequency diagrams and PSR matrices are simultaneously input into the Attention-based Multi-Scale Dilated Convolution Network (A-MSDCNet), leveraging their time-frequency characteristics and nonlinear properties to classify EEGs before and after the application of TENS. The results based on the dataset established by our research institute indicate that the proposed method is superior to existing methods. It achieves optimal performance in various indicators such as average classification accuracy (ACC), standard deviation (STD), Cohen's kappa coefficient (kappa), F1 score (F1), and area under the curve (AUC).

articleTitle: Spatio-Temporal Feature Attention Fusion for Fault Detection in Complex Industrial Processes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: In the practice of maintaining industrial production safety, fault detection in industrial processes plays a crucial role. The data generated during industrial production is influenced by numerous operating conditions, resulting in process data often exhibiting spatiotemporal complexity. Existing fault detection methods face significant challenges in effectively handling these characteristics simultaneously. To address this, this paper proposes a Spatio-temporal Feature Attention Fusion (ST-FAF) framework designed to extract both temporal and spatial features from time-series data. Specifically, the paper utilizes a one-dimensional convolutional neural network to extract spatial features from the raw time-series data, while employing the Gramian Angular Summation Field (GASF) method to convert time-series data into two-dimensional images for better capture of temporal features. Furthermore, a channel weighting mechanism is introduced to enhance the expressive power of both temporal and spatial features. Ultimately, through a cross-fusion strategy, the organic integration of temporal and spatial features is achieved. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through numerical examples and Tennessee-Eastman process. Experimental results confirm that the proposed method outperforms existing technologies in fault detection accuracy, thereby demonstrating its significant application value in the field of industrial safety production.

articleTitle: Joint Task Offloading and Resource Allocation in Software-Defined Networking-Enabled Vehicular Edge Computing: A Multi-Objective Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Vehicular Edge Computing (VEC) enables vehicles to offload computation tasks to edge servers, effectively addressing computing resource constraints faced by vehicles. However, the efficient scheduling of network edge computing resources is crucial in VEC. In this work, we investigate task offloading and resource allocation in Software-Defined Networking (SDN)-enabled VEC to minimize delay and cost by efficiently utilizing resources of vehicles and edge servers. Specifically, we propose a computation offloading architecture in SDN-enabled VEC, where resource-constrained vehicles can offload computation tasks to edge servers. Furthermore, we formulate a joint task offloading and resource allocation problem, which is a non-linear programming problem. Inspired by the advantages of particle swarm optimization (PSO), we propose a PSO-based task offloading and resource allocation algorithm that searches for Pareto-optimal solutions. Finally, we build a simulation model and evaluate the performance comprehensively. The simulation results exhibit the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Time-Series Adjusted FasterPAM Clustering of Enterprise Electricity Consumption Based on Autocorrelation Function
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Analyzing enterprise electricity consumption behav-ior and patterns is crucial for studying the power market. One approach is to use time series clustering to analyze enterprise electricity consumption, allowing for the customization of services to enhance satisfaction for enterprises with similar characteristics and aiding in the detection of abnormal usage to improve electrical safety. However, the significant differences in scale among different enterprises' electricity consumption make direct clustering challenging. Traditionally, features of time series, such as autocorrelation functions, are extracted to classify time series with similar structures. Selecting different lag numbers for the autocorrelation function can lead to varying results, making this selection critically important. This paper proposes a novel time series clustering method based on estimated autocorrelation functions, which automatically selects the appropriate lag number and integrates with the FasterPAM clustering method to enhance computational efficiency. Moreover, since the FasterPAM method requires predefining the number of clusters, we introduce a new index to determine the optimal number of clusters. Thus, the proposed autocorrelation-based adjusted FasterPAM clustering method offers a more automated approach. Finally, we apply this method to real-world data, clustering the monthly electricity consumption of 197 enterprises in a certain province of eastern China, and analyze the structural characteristics of the clustered time series.

articleTitle: Industrial Process Soft Sensing Based on Nonlinear Sparse Generalized Method of Moments Estimation Model and Relevance Vector Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: In industrial processes, soft sensing is widely used to predict key quality variables. Selecting appropriate auxiliary variables is crucial for establishing an accurate soft sensing model. However, current research still faces challenges in balancing accuracy and efficiency in auxiliary variable selection, which affects predictive performance. Therefore, this paper proposes a variable selection method based on the Nonlinear Sparse Generalized Method of Moments (NS-GMM) and integrates it with Relevance Vector Regression (RVR) for soft sensing modeling to achieve precise prediction of key variables. Considering the nonlinear relationships among actual variables, and traditional GMM models are designed for linear problems, the kernel technique is first incorporated into the GMM model to form a nonlinear GMM model. Second, regularization terms are introduced into the nonlinear GMM model to sparsify the model parameters, thereby alleviating the “contamination effect” in variable selection. Furthermore, the parameters of the NS-GMM are used to construct a variable selection criterion to filter out auxiliary variables that have a significant impact on the target variable. Then, the selected auxiliary variables are used to train an RVR model for soft sensing modeling and prediction. Finally, numerical simulations validate the effectiveness of the improved GMM approach. The performance of the proposed method is verified using the penicillin fermentation process. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional methods in both variable selection and prediction performance. This method provides new insights and tools for precise measurement and control in industrial processes.

articleTitle: Analysis and Application of Retail Commodity Consumption Situation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: In the background of the continuous development of information technology and big data, retail enterprises have accumulated massive data. In order to fully use these data and intuitively show the retail market sales situation, this paper proposes a system that combines spatial-temporal grid division, knowledge graph implicit relationship mining and market situation visualization technology. This system firstly associates and integrates external consumer market data with internal sales data through spatial-temporal grid division technology to form a basic data source with time series and geographic space characteristics. Then, the knowledge graph technology is used to mine the implicit relationship among commodities, markets and consumers (CMC). Finally, this paper adopts visualization technology to construct a system that reflects the changes of the retail market and the internal connection among CMC in the field of commodity consumption. The system can provide technical support for big data mining and multi-angle visualization analysis of the retail commodity market.

articleTitle: Task Offloading and Resource Allocation for ICVs in CFNs via Constrained MARL
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Computing First Network (CFN) aims to enable unified scheduling of computing nodes across the network, positioning it as a promising paradigm for managing the computationally intensive tasks of Intelligent Connected Vehicles (ICVs). Given the highly dynamic vehicle network topology and uneven vehicle density, ICV tasks may fail due to limited computing resource on individual node. Thus, it is crucial for CFN to efficiently schedule I CV tasks and allocate resources to ensure their successful completion. However, existing task scheduling methods often struggle with large action spaces and tend to over-look the correlation between offloading and resource allocation decisions. Additionally, the high computing resource demands of ICV tasks require CFN to allocate resources within constrained range to ensure timely overall task completion. To address these challenges, we propose a Constrained and Action Represented Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (CARMARL) framework that generates reliable policies to meet the QoS requirements of I CV tasks while fully utilizing computing resources in CFN. Specifically, CARMARL maintains a Conditional Variational Autoencoder (CVAE) to reduce the action space and enable agents to learn the correlation between offloading and allocation decisions and a Reward Constrained Policy Optimization (RCPO) module to ensure resource allocation remains reasonableness. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CARMARL improves task completion rate by up to 25.2 % compared to all baselines.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Algorithm for Detecting Steel Defects in Small Samples:RBSI-YOLOv8n
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Aiming at the current problems of low efficiency and poor accuracy of steel surface defect detection with few samples, as well as the challenges of large number of existing defect detection model parameters and low detection accuracy, a lightweight small-sample steel defect detection algorithm based on YOLOv8n (RBSI-YOLOv8n) is proposed. The method introduces the receptive field attention RFCBAMConv module, and accordingly optimizes the design of RF-C2f module instead of C2f, which effectively retains the spatial and channel features and suppresses the redundant information in order to improve the detection accuracy; changes the Neck to the BCAFPN-SE structure, which reduces the complexity of the model and better handles the cross-scale feature information, thus improving the detection performance; optimizes the loss function, and designs the The Inner-Shape-IOU loss function is optimized and the loss function is designed to improve the convergence speed and precision of the algorithm under small-sample detection objects Experimentally verified on the NEU-DET steel defect dataset, compared with the YOLOv8n algorithm, the RBSI-YOLOv8n precision rate is improved by 8.6%, the recall rate is improved by 0.7%, and the mAP is improved by 3.4%. It effectively reduces the misdetection rate and leakage rate during the actual detection. And the number of parameters is only 66.7% of the original model, and the computational amount is 95% of the original model, the model is more lightweight and meets the needs of more scenarios. The results show that the algorithm achieves a better balance between detection accuracy and lightweighting under the steel small sample detection object, and provides a reliable reference for edge terminal devices with high accuracy and low computing power deployment.

articleTitle: GarmentFolding:Learning Efficient Garment Folding Based on Lift&Drag Dynamic Action
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: In robotic arm manipulation, folding clothes is highly challenging due to the garments' inherent infinite degrees of freedom. Our designed system can unfold garments from any configuration and automatically center them in the workspace during folding, thereby minimizing constraints on the robotic arm's motion range. High-quality garment unfolding significantly enhances folding efficiency. Therefore, this study introduces a novel action strategy, “Lift&Drag,” which involves high-speed dynamic actions to adjust garments from any state to a prede-fined configuration, ensuring superior unfolding. To bridge the simulation-reality gap and improve fabric keypoint detection ac-curacy, we collected extensive real-world fabric images, creating a dataset of approximately 2,000 images. This dataset notably enhances the performance of fabric folding keypoint detection. Experimental results show that the method reliably performs in real-world settings, achieving 91.3 % unfolding coverage and a 92.8 % folding success rate, particularly with heavily wrinkled t-shirts.

articleTitle: Bi-GRUI and Transformer Variant Based Missing Value Imputation Method for Electricity Consumption Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: The accuracy of electricity consumption data collection has a direct impact on the billing of users. In view of the inevitable existence of some missing data problems in the collection of electricity consumption data of ten million users, especially with the development of time-sharing tariff business, the inconsistency of tariff periods of different user groups and the frequent changes in the collection time period have further reduced the success rate and the completeness rate of electricity consumption data collection. For this reason, this paper proposes a Bi-GRUI and Transformer variant of missing value imputation method for electricity consumption data. The model as a whole utilizes a two-stage imputation method. In the first stage, an AutoEncoder (AE) structure based on Bi-Gated Recurrent Unit Imputation Unit (Bi-GRUI) is used to perform missing value completion of the data after masking operation. Considering the influence of time-sharing tariff influencing factor as well as the time decay factor, which is introduced into the global attention in the decoder, in order to fully excavate the time-sharing variability and the temporal correlation of the consumer electricity consumption data. The second stage further extracts relevant information from different dimensions, such as time and features, by putting the complementary values into the Transformer variant to obtain the final missing value complementary results. The experimental results show that the model proposed in this paper can effectively fit the missing values of user load, which can be used to support the construction of a new generation of collection system.

articleTitle: Enhancing Driver Decision-Making Through Head-Up Display: A Study on Information Sensitivity and Visualization Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: With the increasing integration of advanced on-board sensors and vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication systems in modern vehicles, a wide range of real-time information, such as traffic conditions, can be captured and displayed in intelligent cabins to assist drivers in making driving decision more effectively. However, it remains unclear which types of information are most sensitive to driving behavior and how to effectively visualize them to enhance driver assistance. This work investigates the impact of different information types and methods of presentation on driving behavior. Particularly, we focus on the usage of Head-Up Displays (HUDs) through the method that combines survey and simulation experiments. The survey will first capture drivers' preferences regarding in-formation from the HUD and their subjective assessment of display clarity and effectiveness. Subsequently, we design a simulation-based driving experiment using Webots simulator to evaluate the impact of HUD on driving performance in typical platoon scenarios. Results indicate that, by providing key real-time information such as navigation, speed, and vehicle distance in HUDs, driving stability can be significantly enhanced. The study concludes that HUD is an effective way for improving driver decision-making plan in complex traffic environments, offering insights into optimizing information presentation ways for future intelligent cabin designs.

articleTitle: Cooperative Scheduling and Hierarchical Memory Model for Multi-Agent Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are leading a technological revolution. This gives agents based on LLMs renewed vitality, and multi-agent collaboration is showing the potential to foster new forms of intelligence. However, current multi-agent systems face two major challenges: the first is the issue of resource coordination and scheduling within multi-agent systems, and the second is the limitation of the context window in large models, which hinders the practical application of agents in long-term conversational scenarios, urgently requiring improvements in memory capabilities. To address these challenges, we propose a collaborative scheduling strategy and hierarchical memory model for LLM-based multi-agent systems inspired by operating systems. First, we design a time-sharing scheduling strategy, analogous to process scheduling in operating systems, which divides the resource usage cycle into finer-grained single-step workflows, allocating independent resource windows to different agents to reduce resource contention and conflicts. Second, we introduce a hierarchical memory model based on the multi-level cache architecture of operating systems, segmenting the agents' memory into core memory, main memory, and vague memory areas, thereby significantly improving memory retention and retrieval efficiency in LLM - based agents when handling complex tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method achieves efficient resource allocation in multi-agent systems while significantly enhancing the memory capabilities of agents and overall system performance.

articleTitle: VariSize: A Dataset and Model for $3\mathrm{D}$ Garment Grading and Editing Based on Latent Space
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Product Compliance Engineering - Asia (ISPCE-ASIA)
abstract: Garment size is a critical feature of garments. Traditional resizing usually requires grading 2D sewing patterns according to specific rules and then sewing them together. This process is not only unintuitive but also time-consuming. Some methods aim to achieve a better fit by conforming the garment to the body's shape, which alters the garment structure. To simplify this grading process, we propose an automated 3D garment grading method that changes the garment size while maintaining its original structure. We compress garments into latent codes within a high-dimensional latent space. Then we introduce VFNet and SVNet, VFNet employs a multi-class logistic regression model to generate probabilities for attribute labels mapped to latent vectors. By controlling the weights of garment attributes, it enables feature part editing. SVNet learns the size transformation relationships of garments within the latent space, facilitating 3D garment resizing through label-based adjustments. Due to the lack of datasets containing garments of different sizes, we constructed a dataset called VariSize, which includes five types of garments: T-shirts, cardigans, trousers, dresses, and skirts, with each type having four sizes. Each garment's different parts are labeled accordingly. Experimental results demonstrate that our method successfully achieves automatic 3D garment resizing and feature part editing, offering significant value for 3D virtual try -on and garment design.
